Lexiro MCP Server

All your product documentation right in your IDE. 9 tools, one API key, zero context switching.

MCP Protocol
Internal Processing
Gemini API
PostgreSQL / pgvector
1
Why MCP Server?
A developer is integrating with a device or platform — IP camera, access control, intercom, NVR, VMS, IoT gateway, or any software with a REST/gRPC/SOAP API. The usual workflow: IDE → browser → search PDFs → copy → back to IDE. With Lexiro MCP Server, the AI assistant finds the right endpoints, parameters, and code examples without ever leaving the editor.
What is it
Model Context Protocol — an open standard (by Anthropic) for connecting external data sources to AI assistants in IDEs
Supported IDEs
Cursor VS Code (Copilot) Claude Desktop Windsurf JetBrains AI
Key difference
Web Chat — Lexiro generates the answer itself (Gemini Pro)
MCP Server — Lexiro provides documentation, and your IDE's model uses it to write code
9 tools
Semantic search, exact endpoint lookup, product and document navigation, section reading, code examples, documentation grep
2
Connect in 30 Seconds
Get an API key from Lexiro settings, add the config to your IDE — done. The AI assistant automatically discovers all 9 tools via MCP discovery.
1. Get your API key

Settings → API Keys → Create Key. Keys start with ipx_

2. Add config to .cursor/mcp.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "lexiro": {
      "url": "https://lexiro.io/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ipx_YOUR_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
Config format
One JSON, one URL, one header. No SDKs, installations, or dependencies.
Discovery
IDE sends tools/list → receives schema of all 9 tools with descriptions and parameters → AI knows how to use them
3
Architecture Under the Hood
MCP Server is built on FastMCP SDK and runs inside the main API container. Transport — Streamable HTTP with JSON-RPC 2.0. Authentication — via API key through ASGI middleware.
SDK & Transport
FastMCP from mcp[cli]>=1.0.0
Streamable HTTP at /mcp
Protocol: JSON-RPC 2.0
stateless_http=True, json_response=True
Authentication
mcp/auth_middleware.py
ASGI middleware → Bearer ipx_*
SHA-256 hash → lookup ApiKey → verify Tenant → ContextVar (tenant_id, api_key_id, client_ip)
Security
Key is hashed: only the hash is stored in DB
last_used_at updated on every request
Error → JSON-RPC error {code: -32001}
Nginx (prod)
/mcp → proxy_pass backend:8000
proxy_read_timeout 600s
Buffering disabled
Maintenance → 503 JSON
Deployment
No separate container — MCP is mounted in the main FastAPI app as Mount("/mcp", app=McpApiKeyAuthMiddleware(mcp.streamable_http_app())). Same api container, same uvicorn.
4
9 Tools — Three Groups
Each tool is a function the AI assistant can call. Tool schemas (name, description, parameters) are auto-generated from Python docstrings via FastMCP.
Semantic Search
search_documentation
The main tool. Semantic search across the entire knowledge base. Hybrid search (vector + BM25) with LLM reranking.
query, product?, version?, doc_type?, limit?
get_api_endpoint
Look up documentation for a specific API path. Exact match on heading_path first, then fallback to semantic search.
endpoint, product?
Knowledge Base Navigation
list_products
List all products with document and chunk counts. Filter by category or name.
category?, query?
get_product_info
Product details: manufacturer, versions, doc types, top-level topics.
product
list_documents
List documents for a product with IDs, format, chunk count. Lighter than outline for large bases.
product, doc_type?
get_document_outline
Document table of contents: H1–H6 heading hierarchy with doc_type for each section.
product, document_title?
Targeted Reading
get_section
Full text of a specific document section. For when a search result was truncated.
document_id, heading
get_code_examples
Code examples from documentation. Filter by topic and programming language. Priority: doc_type=example.
product, topic?, language?
grep_docs
Exact text search (ILIKE). For IP addresses, error codes, URLs, hex values — things semantic search can't find.
pattern, product?, document_id?, include_context?
5
How search_documentation Works Inside
The main tool uses the same search engine as Web Chat: product resolution → query embedding → hybrid search → LLM reranking → threshold filtering. But without answer generation — the IDE receives raw documentation.
1. Product Resolution
search/service.py → resolve_product()
Exact match → ID without LLM
Otherwise → Gemini Flash matches against catalog
2. Query Embedding
gemini-embedding-2-preview
1024D, task_type: RETRIEVAL_QUERY
Redis cache: TTL 48 hrs
3. Hybrid Search
Vector: pgvector <=> cosine, HNSW ef_search=128
BM25: ts_rank_cd + tsvector
RRF: k=60, weights 0.7/0.3
4. LLM Reranking
Gemini 2.5 Flash
20 candidates → top 10
JSON array of scores [0.0–1.0]
5. Filtering
rag_min_similarity >= 0.35
rerank_min_score >= 0.3
Result limit: 1–20 (default 10)
Key Difference from Web Chat
No LLM answer generation. search_documentation returns found documentation as text. The IDE's LLM decides how to use it for writing code.
6
Response Formatting for IDE
Each result is formatted into a structured text block with metadata. The response is plain text, optimized for the LLM's context window in the IDE.
Header (_format_mcp_meta)
[1] ProductName | v2.0 | DocTitle > Section [api_reference]
Entities: GET /api/v1/door, POST /api/v1/event
(similarity: 0.87, rerank: 0.92)
Body (_format_mcp_body)
Prefers parent_content (full section)
Dedup by SHA-256 parent hash
Truncation: 12,000 chars (3000 tokens x 4)
Separator
Blocks separated by \n\n---\n\n
Each block: metadata + content
Format is the same for all RAG tools
get_api_endpoint — special
Adds [exact match] or [vector match] to metadata — shows whether endpoint was found exactly or via semantic search
7
Telemetry & Billing
Every tool call is logged into three systems: search analytics, detailed MCP request audit (with sources and timings), and billing. Everything is visible in the admin panel and Grafana.
SearchAnalytics
source = "mcp", tool_name
query, duration_ms, result_count, top_similarity
tenant_id, api_key_id
McpRequestLog
Full audit: request_id, tool_name
All tokens (embedding, rerank, resolve)
All timings (embed_ms, search_ms, rerank_ms, resolve_ms)
sources JSONB — preview of each result
client_ip, user_agent, status, error
Billing
billing/pricing.py
calculate_mcp_cogs/charge
Components: embedding + rerank + resolve + search overhead
Navigation tools: cost = 0 (SQL only)
Monitoring
Grafana MCP Tools dashboard
Admin UI: McpAuditPage
User analytics: /analytics/mcp
8
MCP Server vs Web Chat
Two access channels to the same knowledge base. For developers, MCP Server is the optimal choice: documentation flows directly into your IDE context.
MCP Server
Web Chat
Transport
JSON-RPC 2.0 (Streamable HTTP)
REST + SSE streaming
Authentication
Bearer API key (ipx_*)
Session / tenant cookie
Who generates the answer
LLM in IDE (Cursor, Copilot...)
Gemini 2.5 Pro on backend
Search pipeline
embed → hybrid → rerank → format
rewrite → classify → decompose → search → rerank → context assembly → LLM
Prompts
Not used (raw data)
base.md + type-specific, role overrides
Context format
Plain text with metadata headers
XML blocks <documentation_context>
Streaming
No (one request — one response)
SSE: progress → tokens → sources → done
Billing
embedding + rerank + resolve
embedding + rerank + resolve + LLM generation
✓ Developers: MCP Server — code is written right in the IDE, zero context switching. Managers & analysts: Web Chat — convenient web UI with ready-made answers.
